title: 20 BORING Businesses Almost Nobody Has Started (Every One Still Wide Open)
promo_conflict: No paid relationship is disclosed. A tower lease consultancy intake form is recommended as a free first step, so an undisclosed referral relationship cannot be ruled out.

stated_problem.quote: Landowners assume they have to go and find a carrier. They do not.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Cell carrier land lease
idea.one_liner: Lease part of a property to a mobile carrier for a cell site and collect monthly rent.
idea.offer: Land and site access for a cell carrier installation.
idea.revenue_model: Monthly ground lease; rates depend on the site and number of carriers.

key_quotes.quote: Tier one, you may already own this one, leasing a corner of your land to a cell carrier.

claims.claim: National ground leases are quoted at roughly $500 to $2,500 per month, with a database average of about $900 to $1,300; mature multicarrier sites can pay $7,000 to $8,000.
claims.quote: National ground leases run roughly $500 to $2,500 a month with the industry database average sitting around 900 to$1,300. Mature multicarrier sites can pay 7 to8,000.

claims.claim: The consultancy intake step is described as free and lasting 10 minutes.
claims.quote: Submit your parcel coordinates to a tower lease consulty's landowner intake form. Free 10 minutes.

claims.claim: A $1,000 monthly lease without an annual increase would remain at $1,000 per month after 20 years.
claims.quote: If you ever sign a multi-year lease, land, wall, hanger, storage, anything, find the escalator clause first. $1,000 a month signed today with no annual increase written in is still $1,000 a month in 20 years.

claims.claim: An annual increase of 3 to 5% is described as a normal ask.
claims.quote: 3 to 5% a year is a normal ask. If there is no clause, ask for one before you sign.

acquisition_channels.details: Submit parcel coordinates to a tower lease consultancy intake form; the speaker says tower scouts map coverage gaps and mail landowners.

ideas.delivery: The property owner leases the site; the carrier handles the cell equipment and network operation.

tools: tower lease consultancy landowner intake form

ideas.other_uk_rules: UK telecoms planning, property title and lease arrangements differ from the US examples. Check applicable planning and land rights; any UK cold calling should be screened against TPS/CTPS.

stated_problem.quote: Almost nobody counters the first offer. People think the number mailed to them is the number.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Pipeline and utility easements
idea.one_liner: Negotiate payments from utilities or pipeline operators for easement rights over land.
idea.offer: Rights to cross or use land for utility infrastructure.
idea.revenue_model: Payment for an easement; the transcript gives per-rod and per-acre figures.

key_quotes.quote: First move, search your state's landowner easement guide and ring one county extension office to ask what recent easements near you actually paid.

claims.claim: Payments are quoted at $7 to $40 per rod, or about $2,000 to $4,200 per acre for a permanent easement.
claims.quote: Payments run $7 to $40 per rod, which works out around $2,000 to $4,200 an acre for a permanent easement.

acquisition_channels.details: Research regional rates using the state's landowner easement guide and a county extension office.

ideas.delivery: The landowner negotiates and grants easement rights; the utility or pipeline operator uses the land for infrastructure.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK wayleave, easement and compensation arrangements differ from the US examples; check title, consent and applicable UK land rules.

stated_problem.quote: Everyone assumes the rights were severed from the deed generations ago, so nobody ever looks.
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Mineral rights ownership check
idea.one_liner: Check whether mineral rights remain attached to a property's surface deed; the transcript does not specify a monetization offer.
idea.customer: Not stated; mineral rights owners and potential rights buyers are implied.
idea.offer: Determine whether mineral rights are still attached to the property.
idea.revenue_model: Not stated.

key_quotes.quote: First move, call your county recorder and ask whether the mineral rights under your property are still attached to your surface deed.

claims.claim: A courthouse check is described as free and taking about 15 minutes.
claims.quote: A courthouse check is free and takes about 15 minutes.

claims.claim: A formal title search is quoted at $50 to $150.
claims.quote: A formal title search runs $50 to $150.

acquisition_channels.details: Check courthouse records or call the county recorder to establish ownership.

ideas.delivery: The owner checks property records; any subsequent rights transaction is not described.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK mineral ownership and property title rules differ from the US examples; get a UK title search and specialist advice before relying on the rights.

claims.quote: One municipal marina publishes $75 a foot with power included.
